result.topic_en: Ramanujan derives inequalities for the exponents of the prime factors of a generalised superior highly composite number (for divisor sums of s-th powers), bounding $\epsilon$ and the exponent $a_\lambda$ in terms of $\lambda$, $\epsilon$ and $s$.

where $\lambda \le p_1$. Then from (304) it follows that
$1-\lambda^{-s(1+a_\lambda)} \geqslant (1-\lambda^{-s a_\lambda})\lambda^{\epsilon}$,
(306) or $\lambda^{\epsilon} \le \frac{1-\lambda^{-s(1+a_\lambda)}}{1-\lambda^{-s a_\lambda}}$.
Again let $N' = N\lambda$. Then from (305) we see that
$1-\lambda^{-s(1+a_\lambda)} > \{1-\lambda^{-s(2+a_\lambda)}\}\lambda^{-\epsilon}$
(307) or $\lambda^{\epsilon} > \frac{1-\lambda^{-s(2+a_\lambda)}}{1-\lambda^{-s(1+a_\lambda)}}$.
Now let us suppose that $\lambda = p_1$ in (306) and $\lambda = P_1$ in (307).
Then we see that
(308) $\frac{\log(1+p_1^{-s})}{\log p_1} \geqslant \epsilon > \frac{\log(1+P_1^{-s})}{\log P_1}$.
From this it follows that, if
$0 < \epsilon \le \frac{\log(1+2^{-s})}{\log 2}$,
